From a White Paper to a Working Platform: Peripateticware 2007–2026
trans-unit.target: 白紙から実験的なプラットフォームへ:Peripateticware 2007–2026

trans-unit.source: The paper was written at a moment when 3G hadn't fully rolled out, the iPhone was months away from launch, and "app" wasn't yet a common word. Its predictions — that cell phones would become 1-for-1 classroom devices, that mobile networks would reach remote regions, that GPS would become cheap enough to put in every student's pocket — all came true. The products the paper called for did not.
trans-unit.target: この論文は3Gが完全に導入されていない時期、iPhoneが発表される前の数개월、“アプリ”という言葉自体がまだ一般的ではなかった頃に書かれました。その中での予測—ある紙は、Cell Phoneが1-for-1クラスルームデバイスとなり、モバイルネットワークが偏遠地区に到達することが可能になり、GPSが学生の口のポケットに入れるほど 저렴해진다는 것—全てが事実となった。その紙が提唱した製品は存在하지 않았습니다.

trans-unit.source: The 2007 document named one obstacle it couldn't solve:
trans-unit.target: 2007年にはこれらを解決できないという障壁があるとさえしていました。

trans-unit.source: If students follow their curiosity through real places, learning about arches, barrels, and celestial navigation because they're standing near a cathedral or a harbour, how do you assess what they've learned in a way that satisfies curriculum requirements? How do you produce the spreadsheet of numbers the principal wants while also honouring the complexity of what the student actually understood?
trans-unit.target: それによって学生たちは、アーチやバーレル、天体観測などを学ぶことができます。 캔터ベリー大聖堂や港の近くにいると、학생たちは実際に서 배우는 것을 평가하고 교과과정의 요구사항을 만족시킬 수 있습니다。 학생たちが実際に理解しているものを表現する方法を考えることです。

trans-unit.source: The document left that question open. The school system didn't solve it either. For nearly two decades, "outdoor learning" remained either a vague aspiration or a logistical nightmare — teachers with clipboards, activities that produced no artifact, experiences that disappeared the moment students came back inside.
trans-unit.target: その文書はその問題を残しました。 学校システムもそれを解決していないでしょう。 20年近くにわたって「アウトドアラーニング」はある意味では曖昧な志向だけあるか、またはロジスティクの夜 mareです。 先生たちがクリップボー드を持っている、活動によってアーティファクトを生成しない、体験が室内に戻ってきたときに消える、ということです。

trans-unit.source: The 2026 Answer: AI Did What Spreadsheets Couldn't
trans-unit.target: 答えは2026年、人工智能が出来るものはすべて解決したということです。

trans-unit.source: The assessment problem turned out to have two parts. The first was capturing evidence — what did the student actually observe, and can you prove it? The second was evaluating it — did their thinking deepen, or did they just describe what they saw?
trans-unit.target: 評価問題には二つありました。第一はそれらを証明すること、すなわち学生が実際に何を観察していたか、そしてそれを証明できるか？第二は深化させたということ、あるいはそれを観察しただけということを証明するか？

trans-unit.source: The first part was solved by smartphones. Photo, audio, GPS coordinates, timestamps — a student at a creek bank can capture more evidence in ten minutes than a field trip clipboard could hold in a day. What remained was the second part: structured inquiry that didn't just document experience but deepened it.
trans-unit.target: その後の部分はスマートフォンによって解決されました。 写真や音響、GPSコーディネイト、タイム스탬프などを学生が堰畔の川岸で10分間にわたって撮影することができます。 それ以外は第2部分だけが残りました：規則化された調査を行うことで、体験を深化することができませんか？

trans-unit.source: That's where Peri comes in. Peri is Peripateticware's AI guide — named, like the software, after the Aristotelian method. Peri doesn't answer questions. It asks them. It follows the five-phase inquiry sequence — Engage, Observe, Analyse, Explain, Apply — that Aristotle used in the Lyceum and that cognitive science has since validated as a path to genuine understanding, not just retention. Peri takes a student's observation and asks the next right question. When the student gets it right, Peri tests the implication. When the student is vague, Peri asks for evidence.
trans-unit.target: それには Peri가 있습니다. Peri는 Peripateticware의 AI 가이드로, 소프트웨어의 이름과 같이 아리스토텔레스의 방법에서 따온 이름입니다. Peri는 대답하지 않습니다. 그것은 질문을합니다. 아리스토텔레스가 Lyceum에서 사용한 5 단계 조사 시퀀스 (Engage, Observe, Analyze, Explain, Apply)를 인지 과학이 나중에 진정한 이해로 유도하는 길로 확인했습니다. Peri는 학생의 관찰을 따라가고 다음 올바른 질문을합니다. 학생이 옳은 대답을하면 Peri는 그 결과를 기록합니다. 학생이 모호한 경우 Peri는 증거를 요구합니다.

trans-unit.source: The result is an artifact: a field journal entry with captures, extended analysis, and a record of the inquiry itself. Teachers can see not just what a student concluded but how they got there. Rubrics aligned to Bloom's taxonomy and standards frameworks — CCSS, NGSS, TEKS, or your own — make the assessment legible to any curriculum coordinator. The spreadsheet and the real learning finally occupy the same document.
trans-unit.target: 그 결과는 예술품: 현장 일기에 캡처, 확장된 분석 및 조사 자체의 기록이 포함됩니다. 교사는 학생이 결론을 내린 방법을 보는 것만이 아니라 그들이 어떻게 도착했는지를 볼 수 있습니다. 평가의 레이블을 Bloom의 분류 학과 기준 프레임 워크 (CCSS, NGSS, TEKS, 또는 자신의)로 FERPA 및 COPPA 규정을 준수합니다. 학교 행정부에서 모든 교사와 홈스쿨 학부모가 자신의 활동을 이러한 기준과 일치시킬 수 있습니다. 같은 파일을 재 업로드하면 프로세싱이 건너뛰어집니다 (체크섬 캐시).

trans-unit.source: The 2007 paper described a "choose your own adventure" model of learning — one where students follow tangents, pursue what interests them, and encounter core curriculum concepts through the side doors of genuine curiosity rather than the front door of instruction. The paper acknowledged this was "somewhat chaotic" and that it would require new kinds of instructional design, new assessment tools, and teachers willing to trade some control for authentic engagement.
trans-unit.target: 2007 年の論文には "選択型アドベンチャー"と呼ばれる学습法が記述されています。これは、生徒たちが分岐点を跳ね回り、自己に興味のあるものを追うときに、核心的な学科教育概念をサイド ドアではなく正面入口から出会うことができるようにするものです。論文はこれが"ある程度の混乱を生む"と認めています。そして、新たなタイプの授業設計や評価ツール、学生によって自己が主導権を持つことができるようにする教師が必要であり、また、本来は授業の形式である課程内容をサイド ドアで出会うことができるようにする新しいタイプの学生活動も必要であると述べています。

trans-unit.source: Peripateticware doesn't fully solve the chaos — that tension is real and probably permanent. What it does is give teachers enough structure to stay sane (designed activities, learning targets, completion phases, teacher approval workflows) while giving students enough freedom to actually go somewhere (GPS-triggered content, student-proposed activities, self-directed field notes, peer projects).
trans-unit.target: Peripateticwareは2007年のビジョンを完全に実現するわけではありません。それは、教師が心理的な安定感を保つために必要なだけの構造を持っている一方、学生に自由度を与えて実際にどこかへ行くことができるようにするものです。GPSをトリガーにしたコンテンツや、学生が提案した活動、完了フェイズ、承認ワークフローなどの完成段階を設定しているだけです。

trans-unit.source: The reverse scavenger hunt — where students propose an activity based on something they found — is the closest thing in the platform to that 2007 vision. A student finds a peculiar rock formation. They propose it as an activity. The teacher approves it. Other students go look. Questions emerge that no curriculum document anticipated. Learning moves.
trans-unit.target: リバーススカavengerハントは、学生が発見したものに基づいて活動を提案することが可能なプラットフォーム上では、2007年のビジョンに最便で近いものです。学生が奇異な岩石構造物を発見したら、それを活動として提案することが可能であり、それが批准されると、他の学生たちはそれに詳細を調べます。教科書には予想していなかった質問が出現します。学習が進展していきます。
Example: "このためには 2026 年までかかっているという。"

trans-unit.source: The short answer is that most of the enabling technology wasn't ready in 2007. GPS in every pocket came first (2010–2015). Then high-quality mobile cameras. Then cloud APIs cheap enough for schools. Then local AI models (Ollama, llama.cpp) that can run on a teacher's home server without a $10,000/month inference bill. The 2007 paper was right about the destination; it couldn't have known how long the road would be.
trans-unit.target: Peripateticwareは2007年のビジョンを実現するために必要だった技術が多く欠かっていました。GPSがスマートフォンに装備されるようになった（2010〜2015年）、高画質の携帯用カメラが出現した、クラウドAPIが学校でも使えるほど便宜にて買うことが可能になった（2015〜）。そして、テキストの本体にはAIモデルをローカルに実行させるためのソフトウェアが必要であり、それは教師の家のホームサーバ上でも動作することが可能でした（$10,000/月の認証費用などを支払う代わりに）。2007年の論文は目的地については正しかったが、それが教育技術が解決すべき問題であることを知らなかっただけです。

trans-unit.source: The longer answer is that educational technology spent those years solving the wrong problem. EdTech iterated on the classroom — better LMS, better video, better quiz tools. It made the existing model more efficient. Peripateticware doesn't try to make the classroom more efficient. It tries to replace the classroom, at least occasionally, with the world.
